claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is single-phase BCC.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility and undergoes brittle failure.
A minor Al addition will induce precipitation of a secondary ordered B2 phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The proposed B2 phase will be Al-rich and NiAl-type.
The B2 phase will form a reticulated network along grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
HIP or annealing can facilitate phase separation from an initially single-phase BCC refractory alloy.
The reticulated B2 network will deflect and bridge cracks.
Crack deflection and bridging by the B2 network will prevent catastrophic brittle failure.
The BCC matrix will retain sufficient ductility in the BCC-B2 composite microstructure.
Formation of a secondary phase can increase hardness or compressive strength through precipitation or second-phase strengthening.
Al addition will provide compressive strength comparable to or higher than the baseline.
Al addition and the B2 network will significantly increase room-temperature compressive ductility relative to the baseline.
The modification will cause a marginal increase in density relative to the single-phase BCC baseline.
Although Al is lighter, phase formation or HIP densification may increase the alloy's net density.
Ceramic-reinforced HEAs can gain compressive strength through particle-dislocation interactions and dispersion or second-phase strengthening.
An excessive secondary-phase fraction can form a continuous brittle skeleton and reduce ductility.
Al additions below 5 at.% will promote a beneficial reticulated network without producing a continuous brittle intermetallic skeleton.
Failure to detect B2 at all Al concentrations through 8 at.% would falsify the proposed phase-structure mechanism.
A B2-containing continuous network that lowers fracture strain below baseline without compensating strength would falsify the proposed beneficial-network outcome.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a marginal density increase, but the outcome and uncertainty fields acknowledge that Al is lighter and characterize the net density change as uncertain or potentially negligible. No definite direction is maintained consistently.
